title: Remove Selected Characters
statement:
Remove all characters from a text when they appear in a separate removal set.

Contract
- `text` and `remove` are non-null strings. Either may be empty.
- Treat `remove` as a set of Java `char` values: duplicates in `remove` do not change the result.
- Return a new string containing the characters from `text` whose value is not present in `remove`, preserving their original order.
- Matching is case-sensitive. Do not mutate either input.

Examples
- `removeSelected("Battle of the Vowels: Hawaii vs. Grozny", "aeiou")` returns `"Bttl f th Vwls: Hw vs. Grzny"`.
- `removeSelected("abracadabra", "ab")` returns `"rcdr"`.
- `removeSelected("keep", "xyz")` returns `"keep"`.

examples.input: text = "Battle of the Vowels: Hawaii vs. Grozny", remove = "aeiou"
examples.output: "Bttl f th Vwls: Hw vs. Grzny"

hints: Checking every removal character for every text character works but repeats the same membership question.
Precompute which characters should be removed, then scan the text once and append only the survivors.
A boolean lookup table or set gives constant-time membership checks; the returned string stores the survivors. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space including the output.
inputSyntax: Input: text, then removal characters separated by |, for example: abracadabra|ab
